WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You grew up in a single-parent home, dropped out in 9th grade, and ran with the wrong crowd. Reading and writing were your lifelines, and a youth program became the first place you discovered you could lead and contribute. From there, you set your sights on college — not as a straight line, but as a long, hard-fought climb.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
Even as you were building toward something better, life kept pulling you back. You went to prison three times. You were accepted to UC Berkeley, and in your very first semester, your father was shot in the head and your cousin was found dead in jail. The weight of that grief sent you backward — another arrest, a case where the system wanted to give you seventeen years for something that warranted three. You served three months on an ankle monitor and went back to school.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
Back at UC Berkeley, you threw yourself into research and leadership. You and fellow students analyzed community surveys tied to a proposed police headquarters and training facility, found them to be flawed, and helped ignite the Stop Cop Campus movement. When you realized the people most affected by that research were too impacted for you to build your honors project on their trauma, you stepped back — and started building something else. You developed a theory you call the Digital Factory, describing how lived experience gets converted into commercialized data that surveils and labels people. That theory became the foundation for SEEN: Safety Community Empowerment Network, a community-controlled infrastructure and app you developed not through formal tech training, but through years of research, activism, and documentary filmmaking.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
SEEN is not just an app — it is a functioning infrastructure. It documents interactions with law enforcement, sends real-time safety notifications to trusted contacts so loved ones know exactly where you are and can watch the interaction as it happens, allows users to file complaints through the network rather than through the police directly, and applies AI trained on policies and procedures from California precincts to hold law enforcement accountable while protecting the person in the interaction. The idea was seeded by your relationship with your mother — her worry about you while you were away — and grew into something that addresses a gap that major tech companies have been unwilling to fill. You also created a documentary about this work, learning production firsthand along the way.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

ACT 5: THE LEGACY
Your mission is to break the loop — to give communities the tools to document, protect, and advocate for themselves rather than be watched, labeled, and left behind by the systems that were supposed to serve them. SEEN is bigger than an app. It is a movement toward community-controlled safety, accountability, and digital equity for the people who have historically had the least access to all three. You describe taking a chance on you as taking a chance on hope — and you mean it as a collective promise, not just a personal one.
This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

YOUR THING
The most memorable brands become known for one thing.
One clear idea.
One clear promise.
One clear mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe the territory your brand has the opportunity to own is:
"Community-controlled safety technology built from lived experience and research"
This becomes the foundation of authority.
The thing people remember.
The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

THE MISSION YOU ARE BUILDING
The strongest brands don't simply sell services.
They stand for something.
They fight against something.
They create movements.
Based on our review, we believe your mission includes:
✓ You believe that people who have been failed by systems — incarceration, surveillance, institutional neglect — deserve tools that protect them rather than further expose them.
✓ You stand for closing the digital divide, especially for formerly incarcerated people and others who lack the foundation to navigate technology that was not built with them in mind.
✓ You believe accountability must be community-driven, not dependent on the goodwill of the same institutions that caused harm — which is why SEEN puts documentation and complaint power directly in people's hands.
✓ You are committed to building bridges between lived experience and systemic change, refusing to extract value from other people's trauma and insisting instead on creating with and for impacted communities.
✓ You believe that the stories of people left behind by larger systems are not footnotes — they are the most important stories to tell, and telling them publicly is itself an act of advocacy.
This is bigger than marketing.
This is bigger than business.
This is legacy.

WHY THIS STORY MATTERS NOW
We live in a world where consumers have more choices than ever before.
The challenge isn't having the best product.
The challenge is being remembered.
People buy from brands they trust.
People trust brands they remember.
People remember stories.
This is why your story matters.
Not because it is interesting.
Because it has the potential to build trust at scale.

For you, specifically, that can look like:

➔ Reaching the People Who Need SEEN Most: You identified that many of the people you most want to help are not reachable through traditional tech channels — they need something visual and human. A documentary can help bridge that gap by making your work accessible to audiences who would never encounter it through an app store or a press release.

➔ Building Trust Before the Download: Safety technology lives or dies on trust. Being seen on a platform that tells your full story — where you came from, what you built, and why — can help potential users and community partners understand not just what SEEN does, but why you are the person who built it, which may strengthen the credibility your mission requires.

➔ Opening Doors to Investors and Collaborators: You noted that large tech companies have been unwilling to support this kind of work. A documented, visible story of SEEN's purpose and functionality can help attract the kind of impact-focused investors and partners who need to see your mission clearly articulated before they will engage.

➔ Amplifying the Advocacy, Not Just the App: SEEN is part of a broader theory — the Digital Factory — and a broader movement around community safety and police accountability. CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Cast Name: Zeke Seaton

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, business background, accomplishments, personality, and overall fit, our casting team believes you could be a strong fit for an upcoming reality show on Inside Success TV.
Our reality shows feature successful entrepreneurs, business owners, founders, and high-performing personalities who are willing to put their experience, decision-making, leadership, and business skills to the test.

Based on our initial review, we believe you have several of the qualities our production team is looking for.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the Inside Success TV casting process.

WHY YOU STOOD OUT
Building a successful business takes a certain type of person.
Reality television adds another layer.
We are looking for entrepreneurs who have already proven themselves in the real world and are willing to see how their skills perform when the environment changes, the pressure increases, and cameras are capturing the experience.
Your application stood out because of the combination of your:
✓ Business experience
✓ Track record
✓ Personality
✓ Decision-making style
✓ Competitive potential
✓ Unique life and business experience
Our team believes these qualities could translate into a compelling presence on an Inside Success TV reality show.

WHY OUR REALITY SHOWS ARE DIFFERENT
Inside Success TV develops reality concepts built around entrepreneurship, competition, strategy, relationships, leadership, and real-world business ability.
Depending on the show, contestants may be asked to:
✓ Build businesses
✓ Generate revenue
✓ Sell or market products
✓ Complete entrepreneurial challenges
✓ Lead teams
✓ Compete against other successful entrepreneurs
✓ Make decisions with limited time or resources
✓ Adapt to unfamiliar environments
✓ Work with unexpected partners
✓ Put their business instincts to the test
The exact format varies by production, but the goal remains consistent:
Put successful people into situations where their skills, personalities, and decision-making are tested in ways they may never have experienced before.
Experience matters.
Strategy matters.
Personality matters.
Execution matters.

YOUR COMPETITIVE PROFILE
Based on what we learned during the application process, our casting team currently sees several qualities that could make you an interesting addition to an upcoming production.
BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
You built your way up from blue-collar roots in the mountains of western North Carolina, moving through welding, mill work, and mining before earning your home inspection license and launching your own inspection company, which you later sold. From there, you created two separate companies: one focused on air remediation and moisture, and a dedicated radon company with its own national certification. At 30 years old, you now run a team of 8 employees organized into 4 crews with a manager, and you have been off job sites entirely for 8 months, supported by virtual assistants handling incoming calls while you focus on growth and networking.
COMPETITIVE EDGE
Your strongest edge is the rare combination of hands-on technical expertise and the systems thinking needed to step back from daily operations. Because you hold your home inspection credentials alongside your remediation work, you describe yourself as a one-stop shop: not just fixing moisture and mold problems, but identifying and addressing their root causes, which you say sets you apart from competitors. You have also demonstrated the ability to build and delegate, structuring your team and hiring support staff to free yourself up for higher-level growth activities.
PERSONALITY
You come across as self-aware, grounded, and genuinely humble, noting openly that you were raised without money and have built everything you have from scratch. You listen more than you talk, something you stated directly and backed up with how you serve as a translator between your marketing-focused business partner and your field contractors. Your energy is easy and confident without being boastful, and you balance a competitive, physically active lifestyle, including daily gym training, bodybuilding, hunting, and hiking, with a clear drive to help others succeed, citing workout programs you built for people at no charge and peptides you sold to help people with weight loss.
THE WILDCARD
What could make you unpredictable on a show like Entrepreneurs Island is the contrast between your collaborative, listen-first instincts and the competitive environment the show creates. You have described wanting to be the least knowledgeable person in any room so you can absorb from those around you, a mindset that could make you a natural alliance builder in team challenges while keeping others from reading you as a threat. Your background as a former bull rider, combined with a blue-collar toughness shaped by working seven days a week in mines and on job sites, suggests you may surprise other cast members when physical or high-pressure challenges arise.
These are some of the qualities our production team will explore further during the next stage of casting.

THE REAL QUESTION
Building a successful company proves that you know how to perform in your current environment.
Reality television asks what happens when that environment suddenly changes.
Can you still sell?
Can you still lead?
Can you still make money?
Can you still make strong decisions?
Can you adapt when your original plan falls apart?
Can you work with people who think completely differently from you?
Can you compete against other successful entrepreneurs?
Can you handle being pushed outside your normal routine?
And can you do it while cameras capture the experience?
Those are the moments that Hollywood loves and can make great television.

YOUR AUTHORITY ASSET
In addition to your participation in the reality show, you will also receive a professionally produced documentary-style feature focused on your business, story, expertise, and journey.
Most businesses create content.
Very few create true authority assets.
Your documentary is designed to become a long-term piece of media you can continue using well beyond the show itself.
It has the potential to become:
✓ A trust-building asset
✓ A credibility asset
✓ A sales asset
✓ A speaking asset
✓ A recruitment asset
✓ A referral asset
✓ A PR asset
✓ A social media asset
✓ A personal brand asset
✓ A legacy asset
The reality show gives audiences the chance to see you perform.
The documentary gives them the chance to understand who you are, what you have built, and why your story matters.
Together, they create a powerful foundation for building visibility, credibility, and authority around your brand.

This is how industry fame is built.

INSIDE SUCCESS TV
CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Macca Edwards
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You grew up in a family environment marked by emotional instability, and you learned early to manage everyone else's comfort before your own. People-pleasing became your survival skill, and for years it worked — until it didn't. By 36, you had poured yourself into building your husband's career and raising your children, and somewhere in all of that giving, you lost yourself. Depression moved in quietly, and the light you were born with grew dim.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
Then your dad died. And grief has a way of stripping everything unnecessary away. In the wake of that loss, you came face to face with a truth you could no longer outrun: you had been performing your life instead of living it. You had spent years making yourself smaller so others could feel bigger, and the cost was your own identity, your joy, and at some points, your will to stay. The hardest year of your life became the beginning of the most honest one.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
The path back to yourself did not come through a dramatic single moment — it came through color. What you wore started to change how you felt, and how you felt started to change how you showed up. You began to understand that fashion is not vanity; it is language. It is armor. It is an invitation for connection. You built Mac and Color not as a business plan but as a belief — that what you put on your body changes what you believe about yourself. You started dressing in a way that made strangers in airports lift their heads. You wore pink and cherries and patch jackets with patches that made people laugh out loud, and suddenly conversations were happening, and people were coming alive in front of you. You were proving your thesis one interaction at a time.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
The proof is not in a revenue number or a media mention — it is in the moment a stranger's eyes come up from the ground. It is in the conversation that starts because of what you are wearing. You have watched people come alive through a piece of clothing, and you now know with certainty that color is not decoration — it is medicine. You built a brand rooted in that truth, and you carry a catchphrase that holds the whole mission in five words: dress cute, tell the truth. That is not a tagline. That is a worldview earned through real loss and real resurrection.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

ACT 5: THE LEGACY
The mission of Mac and Color is bigger than clothing. At a moment when the country feels heavy — when people walk through airports in gray with their heads down — you are building a movement around visibility, vibrancy, and permission to be fully alive. You want people to know they can go from feeling like they don't matter, from serving everyone else at the expense of themselves, through the hardest moments imaginable, and arrive somewhere beautiful. Living in color means living honestly. And you are determined to prove that the most beautiful things can grow straight out of the worst experiences — if you are willing to look for them, grab onto them, and leap.
This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

YOUR THING
The most memorable brands become known for one thing.
One clear idea.
One clear promise.
One clear mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe the territory your brand has the opportunity to own is:
"The color-driven movement teaching people to dress honestly and live fully"
This becomes the foundation of authority.
The thing people remember.
The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

THE MISSION YOU ARE BUILDING
The strongest brands don't simply sell services.
They stand for something.
They fight against something.
They create movements.
Based on our review, we believe your mission includes:
✓ You believe dimming your light to make others comfortable is a form of self-betrayal — and that the world needs you at full brightness.
✓ You stand for the idea that fashion is not superficial — what you put on your body changes what you believe about yourself and what you give to the world.
✓ You fight for the people who have spent years performing their lives for others and are ready to start living their own.
✓ You believe the hardest moments are not obstacles to a beautiful life — they are the raw material it is built from, and they deserve to be spoken aloud.
✓ You are building toward a world where color becomes a catalyst for community — where a jacket, a pair of earrings, or a patch with a punchline can lift someone's eyes and remind them they are still here.
This is bigger than marketing.
This is bigger than business.
This is legacy.

WHY THIS STORY MATTERS NOW
We live in a world where consumers have more choices than ever before.
The challenge isn't having the best product.
The challenge is being remembered.
People buy from brands they trust.
People trust brands they remember.
People remember stories.
This is why your story matters.
Not because it is interesting.
Because it has the potential to build trust at scale.

For you, specifically, that can look like:

➔ Visibility for a Brand Still Finding Its Audience: Mac and Color is in its startup phase, and the challenge right now is getting your story and your mission in front of people who need it. A documentary feature can help increase visibility well beyond what organic social reach alone may support, putting your brand in front of audiences who would never have found you otherwise.

➔ Authority That Goes Beyond the Product: You are not just selling clothing — you are selling a philosophy about grief, identity, and aliveness. Being seen on a credible platform can help position you as a voice and a category of one, so that when people encounter Mac and Color, they encounter a mission they want to be part of, not just a product they might buy.

➔ A Story That Creates Community: You have already watched strangers come alive in airports and stores when they encounter your energy and your color. A documentary can extend that moment to a much wider audience, helping attract the kind of people who are ready to be seen, lifted, and connected — and who may become loyal supporters of everything you build.

➔ Credibility That Supports Future Growth: As you grow Mac and Color, having a documented story — one that captures the why behind the brand — can help strengthen conversations with potential collaborators, press, and partners. It gives people a way to understand and trust you before they ever meet you.

➔ A Platform That Matches the Moment: You described a country that feels sad, heads down, craving vibrancy. Your message — dress cute, tell the truth, live in color — is precisely the kind of counter-narrative that can resonate right now. Sharing it on a larger platform has the potential to reach people at exactly the moment they most need to hear it.

We do not guarantee exact outcomes - results may vary!

Most businesses create content.
Very few create authority assets.
A documentary is not simply content.
It becomes an asset that can be used for years.
Your episode has the potential to become:

✓ A credibility asset
✓ A speaking asset
✓ A sales asset
✓ A recruitment asset
✓ A referral asset
✓ A PR asset
✓ A social media asset
✓ A personal brand asset
✓ A legacy asset
The documentary becomes the foundation.
Everything else is built around it.

YOUR FAME STACK
One story can become hundreds of authority-building opportunities.
From a single episode we can create:
✓ Social media content
✓ Podcast content
✓ PR opportunities
✓ Blog content
✓ Speaking opportunities
✓ Website content
✓ Sales assets
✓ Recruitment assets
✓ Thought leadership content
✓ Future media opportunities
The episode is not the destination.
It is the beginning.
One story.
Distributed everywhere.
Repeated consistently.
This is how authority is built.
This is how industry fame is built.

WHY WE BELIEVE YOU ARE A FIT
We believe your story has the potential to:
✓ Educate others
✓ Inspire others
✓ Build trust
✓ Strengthen your authority
✓ Increase your visibility
✓ Position you as a leader within your category
Most importantly...
We believe your story deserves to be told.

NEXT STEP
Your application has now advanced to the next stage of casting.
During your next call we will discuss:
• Your story in greater detail
• The vision for your episode
• Potential positioning opportunities
• Distribution strategy
• Authority-building opportunities
• Whether this is the right fit for both parties
Please ensure you attend your next scheduled call.
Failure to attend may result in your application being withdrawn from the current casting cycle.

IMPORTANT
Conditional approval expires on:
Sunday 11.59pm EST
After this deadline your application may need to be re-reviewed by casting before being reconsidered for a future season.

WHY YOU STOOD OUT
Building a successful business takes a certain type of person.
Reality television adds another layer.
We are looking for entrepreneurs who have already proven themselves in the real world and are willing to see how their skills perform when the environment changes, the pressure increases, and cameras are capturing the experience.
Your application stood out because of the combination of your:
✓ Business experience
✓ Track record

✓ Decision-making style
✓ Competitive potential
✓ Unique life and business experience
Our team believes these qualities could translate into a compelling presence on an Inside Success TV reality show.

WHY OUR REALITY SHOWS ARE DIFFERENT
Inside Success TV develops reality concepts built around entrepreneurship, competition, strategy, relationships, leadership, and real-world business ability.
Depending on the show, contestants may be asked to:
✓ Build businesses
✓ Generate revenue
✓ Sell or market products
✓ Complete entrepreneurial challenges
✓ Lead teams
✓ Compete against other successful entrepreneurs
✓ Make decisions with limited time or resources
✓ Adapt to unfamiliar environments
✓ Work with unexpected partners
✓ Put their business instincts to the test
The exact format varies by production, but the goal remains consistent:
Put successful people into situations where their skills, personalities, and decision-making are tested in ways they may never have experienced before.
Experience matters.
Strategy matters.
Personality matters.
Execution matters.

YOUR COMPETITIVE PROFILE
Based on what we learned during the application process, our casting team currently sees several qualities that could make you an interesting addition to an upcoming production.
BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
You built a hospitality group from the ground up, currently operating four locations across Tennessee, including Noir Kitchen and Cocktails, an upscale soul food restaurant in Nashville, a nightclub called Link Social Kitchen, a franchise lounge location in Murfreesboro, and a recently signed partnership with a juice and smoothie concept called Alchemy Cafe. Your path to this point was anything but straight: you launched your first food concept with roughly five thousand dollars, worked through a business failure when a lack of a liquor license made the model unsustainable, and deliberately humbled yourself by working at IHOP for six to eight weeks specifically to learn breakfast operations. From there you ran ghost kitchens on platforms like Uber Eats and DoorDash for about two years before moving into club kitchen roles at venues including Minerva and 3000 Bar, and eventually securing your own liquor license and opening what has become one of Nashville's most recognized restaurant brands. You noted that a chef within Nashville's culinary community told you only two restaurants in the market generate more revenue than yours, and you described averaging around one hundred twenty-five thousand dollars a week in revenue.
COMPETITIVE EDGE
Your strongest demonstrated skills are resourcefulness and marketing, both of which show up repeatedly across your story. When your first concept struggled, you did not exit the industry; you found a lower-overhead path through ghost kitchens and delivery platforms to stay in the game and keep sharpening your craft. On the marketing side, you built Noir Kitchen and Cocktails to approximately fifty-five thousand Instagram followers and described a clear strategic instinct around audience diversification, articulating a goal to move the brand beyond its current primary community base and position it as one of a well-regarded restaurants in Tennessee, not just the best Black-owned option. You also showed genuine competitive awareness, referencing a comparable hospitality concept with ten locations and stating you would expand strategically into markets where that competitor is not already operating.
PERSONALITY
On the call you came across as grounded, self-aware, and quietly confident, a combination that tends to read well on camera. You were candid about your own gaps, openly admitting you are somewhat shy on social media and that you are not yet ready for a chef competition format, while in the same breath expressing genuine confidence that you can compete with entrepreneurs at a high level. That honesty about where you are versus where you are going gives you a believable arc rather than a polished pitch, and your humor surfaced naturally when you described getting frustrated on a ten-thousand-dollar brunch day and wondering where all the customers were.
THE WILDCARD
The tension between your quiet, reserved personal brand and the scale of what you have actually built could make you genuinely unpredictable in a group setting like this show. You described yourself as shy and someone who does not post much personally, yet you are running four hospitality locations and generating the kind of weekly revenue that ranks near the top of your market. In a mansion full of entrepreneurs who may lead with loud personal brands, your low-profile style paired with real operational experience could either position you as an underestimated strategic player or create friction if the challenges demand visible charisma and salesmanship. Your background moving fluidly between promotion, cooking, ghost kitchens, and club operations also suggests you may adapt quickly to unfamiliar challenge formats, though how you perform when taken entirely outside your hospitality comfort zone is the real unknown.
These are some of the qualities our production team will explore further during the next stage of casting.

THE REAL QUESTION
Building a successful company proves that you know how to perform in your current environment.
Reality television asks what happens when that environment suddenly changes.
Can you still sell?
Can you still lead?
Can you still make money?
Can you still make strong decisions?
Can you adapt when your original plan falls apart?
Can you work with people who think completely differently from you?
Can you compete against other successful entrepreneurs?
Can you handle being pushed outside your normal routine?
And can you do it while cameras capture the experience?
Those are the moments that Hollywood loves and can make great television.

INSIDE SUCCESS TV
CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Sierra Nova
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You built your skills from the ground up, earning your cosmetology degree, your barber's license, your esthetician license, and ultimately your instructor's license — every credential available in your field in the state of Missouri. But the path wasn't comfortable. Working under others meant long hours that didn't bend for motherhood, ideas that weren't welcomed, and income that felt like pennies on the dollar for the value you brought in. You were always too ambitious, too outspoken, too full of vision for a seat that wasn't yours.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...

You built your foundation in the hospitality world the hard way, starting in restaurants at 17 and working your way up through hotels, event management, and food and beverage leadership. The turning point came when graduate school forced a choice: you could not sustain full-time institutional work and pursue growth at the same time. And it was the beginning of something that would become entirely yours.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
You auditioned for MasterChef in a blind tasting in Orlando, made it through multiple rounds, and went head-to-head with someone who would go on to place second in the competition, all without classical training. You later taught hospitality and tourism management as a professor for six years, sharing everything you had learned with no gatekeeping. Then came the harder tests: postpartum heart failure dropped your heart function to ten percent, and doctors questioned how you were still standing. You changed your diet, committed to your health, and rebuilt. Through all of it, you kept cooking, kept teaching, kept showing up.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
Today your catering business runs full-time with a team of about fifteen people. You have been booked continuously since leaving your teaching contract, staying busy through the year and into the next. Your heart function has recovered to around fifty percent, a result your doctors describe as remarkable. You teach courses and classes on healing through food, speak at engagements, and mentor the next generation with the same generosity that was shown to you. The business that started as a side hustle is now your full-time mission, and it is growing faster than word of mouth alone can carry.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

You auditioned for MasterChef in a blind tasting in Orlando, made it through multiple rounds, and went head-to-head with someone who would go on to place second in the competition, all without classical training. You later taught hospitality and tourism management as a professor for six years, sharing everything you had learned with no gatekeeping. Then came the harder tests: postpartum heart failure dropped your heart function to ten percent, and doctors questioned how you were still standing. You changed your diet, committed to your health, and rebuilt. Through all of it, you kept cooking, kept teaching, kept showing up.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

Today your catering business runs full-time with a team of about fifteen people. You have been booked continuously since leaving your teaching contract, staying busy through the year and into the next. Your heart function has recovered to around fifty percent, a result your doctors describe as remarkable. You teach courses and classes on healing through food, speak at engagements, and mentor the next generation with the same generosity that was shown to you. The business that started as a side hustle is now your full-time mission, and it is growing faster than word of mouth alone can carry.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

You are building toward something larger than a catering calendar: a movement rooted in the belief that food heals, that generosity multiplies, and that a single person's survival story can change how others eat, live, and think about what is possible. This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

One clear promise.
One clear mission.

"The chef who heals communities through food, story, and radical generosity"
This becomes the foundation of authority.

The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

They fight against something.

CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Nathan Dotson
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You grew up watching your father build cabinets as a hobby, then take the leap into running his own shop when you were in high school. That world of wood, craft, and hand-built precision became the air you breathed long before you ever thought of it as a career. When you graduated, the path forward wasn't clear, and college felt more like a placeholder than a destination.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
While you were at Mankato State University, your parents went through a difficult divorce, and your father was struggling with a serious substance abuse issue. He entered treatment, and suddenly the business he had built was without a steady hand at the wheel. At 23 years old, you faced a defining moment: step in and take over, or watch everything your family had built come undone.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
You dropped out of college, set aside any uncertainty about your direction, and took the reins of the business. There was no roadmap, no degree, and no guarantee — only the craft your father had taught you and the drive you had to figure the rest out. Over the next three decades, you taught yourself what the classroom never offered, built a reputation entirely on the quality of your work, and grew a client base that spans designers, contractors, and wholesale partners across the region and beyond.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
Today you run a family business that is busier than you care to be — your words. You have never needed to advertise, because referrals and reputation have carried the work. You serve the Minneapolis market as your primary base and have completed projects as far as Florida and Utah for designers and contractors who seek you out specifically. A designer you have worked with for many years had a project recognized with an ASID award. Your two sons now work alongside you, carrying the craft into another generation.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

ACT 5: THE LEGACY
You are not just building cabinets — you are making a case that a life of skill, discipline, and self-determination is a legitimate and worthy path. You believe too many young people are steered toward a four-year degree that leaves them in debt and without direction, when trades and craftsmanship offer something real. Your mission is to show students and young people that success does not require a diploma — it requires drive, and that custom woodworking, as a dying art, deserves to be seen, valued, and passed on.
This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

YOUR THING
The most memorable brands become known for one thing.
One clear idea.
One clear promise.
One clear mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe the territory your brand has the opportunity to own is:
"The college dropout who built a craft business on skill, not a degree"
This becomes the foundation of authority.
The thing people remember.
The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

THE MISSION YOU ARE BUILDING
The strongest brands don't simply sell services.
They stand for something.
They fight against something.
They create movements.
Based on our review, we believe your mission includes:
✓ You believe a college degree is not the only path to a successful, self-sufficient life — and you have lived that truth for thirty years.
✓ You stand for the trades as a legitimate and respected career, at a time when skilled craftsmen are sorely lacking and the art of custom woodworking is quietly disappearing.
✓ You are fighting to change the story young people are told — that without a diploma, their options are limited — because your life proves otherwise.
✓ You believe discipline, self-motivation, and a willingness to do the work are more reliable foundations for success than any institution can provide.
✓ You are building a legacy that runs in the family, passing the craft and the values behind it to the next generation, one project at a time.
This is bigger than marketing.
This is bigger than business.
This is legacy.

WHY THIS STORY MATTERS NOW
We live in a world where consumers have more choices than ever before.
The challenge isn't having the best product.
The challenge is being remembered.
People buy from brands they trust.
People trust brands they remember.
People remember stories.
This is why your story matters.
Not because it is interesting.
Because it has the potential to build trust at scale.

➔ Visibility Without Advertising: You have built your business entirely on referrals, but a documentary can help extend your reputation beyond your existing network — giving designers, contractors, and wholesale partners across the country a way to discover and trust your work before they ever make a call.

➔ Authority in a Dying Art: Custom woodworking is, in your own words, a dying art. Being documented as a master of that craft can help position you as the standard-bearer for the category — someone worth seeking out, not just someone who comes up in a referral.

➔ A Story That Travels: You already work in Florida, Utah, and beyond for clients who find you worth the distance. A visible, shareable media asset can help those far-reach relationships grow more naturally, giving future clients a reason to trust you before geography becomes a question.

➔ A Message Bigger Than the Business: Your story — dropout to thirty-year craftsman and business owner — speaks directly to the conversation happening right now about college, trades, and what success actually looks like. That message has the potential to resonate far beyond your industry and connect you with audiences who are ready to hear it.

➔ A Platform for the Next Generation: With your sons already working alongside you and a mission to show young people that the trades are a real path forward, a documentary can help amplify that message in a way that word of mouth alone cannot — giving your legacy a stage that lasts.

INSIDE SUCCESS TV
CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Jason
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You left home at 15 and spent years figuring out your place in the world without a conventional map. You went to Job Corps, earned your GED, and stumbled into the sign and graphics trade not through a plan but through a chance encounter — your sketchbook sitting open in the right place at the right moment. From the beginning, you straddled two worlds: a kid raised in a well-off area with divorced parents who also knew what it meant to move through harder circles without flinching.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
The turning point wasn't a business plan — it was betrayal. A partnership that was supposed to launch your career went sideways, and the anger that followed became the fuel. You had always had the ability; what you lacked was the proof that you could do it alone. Fear was the real obstacle, and it took someone else's bad faith to finally push you past it and start your own shop.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
What followed was anything but linear. You went back to school as a graphic artist as computer graphics were just emerging, worked your way through different corners of the industry, and eventually landed at the New York Times before the economy shifted and pulled you back to signs and wraps. Through a divorce, single parenthood with majority custody of your kids, and the financial turbulence of recent years, you kept the business alive — not by scaling aggressively, but by staying sharp, staying adaptable, and treating every job as a craft problem worth solving. You built a second company, a casket-wrapping venture started in 2016, out of a niche no one else was taking seriously, and grew it from a local funeral home in Palm Beach to shipping wrapped caskets outside of Florida.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.

v2_1793961705217_fuafe0ws.draft_text:
INSIDE SUCCESS TV
CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Jeremy Smith
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You built your foundation the hard way — 16 years as a head superintendent for a steel erection company in Atlanta, Georgia, overseeing megastructures, stadiums, high-rises, and bridges. You became the person other people depended on to get the impossible done, and you were exceptionally good at it. But the work was always someone else's legacy, not yours.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
After 16 years of making someone else's business grow, the moment came when the value you created wasn't being matched by what you were offered in return. Rather than accept that, you walked away. Your wife asked what you were going to do, and your answer was simple: the same work, but this time for yourself. That decision required everything.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
You launched your own company and quickly learned that deep expertise and low overhead were a powerful combination — you could price competitively and still deliver at a level that larger contractors couldn't match. Word spread through the quality of your work, not through ad budgets. Early advertising through social media, local print, and a billboard produced modest returns, but the clients who saw your projects firsthand kept calling back. You also navigated the tension every serious tradesperson faces: balancing the demands of building a business against securing your long-term financial foundation, which eventually led you to step back from active bidding for a period to protect your pension credits.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
The proof of what you built isn't just in contracts won — it's in the scale of what you've touched. You worked on landmark projects, including a historically significant development at the Surf Club in North Miami, where the original structure was preserved as part of a Four Seasons hotel. Even after stepping back from active business development, the calls never stopped. Clients still want you back. That kind of demand doesn't follow someone who was average — it follows someone who set a standard others couldn't replicate.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

ACT 5: THE LEGACY
You're not chasing the next job. You're thinking in decades — building something that could be passed to one of your five children, sold as a proven and trusted business, or grown into something you couldn't yet predict. At a point in your career where most people would coast, you're asking how to build something that outlasts the grind. That's not a retirement plan. That's a legacy in progress.
This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

YOUR THING
The most memorable brands become known for one thing.
One clear idea.
One clear promise.
One clear mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe the territory your brand has the opportunity to own is:
"The ironworker who builds businesses as strong as the structures he raised"
This becomes the foundation of authority.
The thing people remember.
The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

THE MISSION YOU ARE BUILDING
The strongest brands don't simply sell services.
They stand for something.
They fight against something.
They create movements.
Based on our review, we believe your mission includes:
✓ Quality and trust are earned on the job site, not in a marketing campaign — and that standard should never be compromised.
✓ Blue-collar expertise deserves the same visibility and respect as any other form of professional leadership.
✓ A business built on craft and reputation is worth protecting, growing, and eventually passing on — not just collecting a check and walking away.
✓ Real family security isn't just financial — it's leaving behind something with your name on it that still stands long after you step back.
✓ The trades have produced some of the most significant structures in this country, and the people behind that work deserve to be known for it.
This is bigger than marketing.
This is bigger than business.
This is legacy.

WHY THIS STORY MATTERS NOW
We live in a world where consumers have more choices than ever before.
The challenge isn't having the best product.
The challenge is being remembered.
People buy from brands they trust.
People trust brands they remember.
People remember stories.
This is why your story matters.
Not because it is interesting.
Because it has the potential to build trust at scale.

For you, specifically, that can look like:

➔ Reaching Clients You Haven't Found Yet: Early advertising through local channels produced limited results for you, while word of mouth carried the weight. A documentary can help extend that trust-based reach to commercial clients, contractors, and homeowners who have never heard your name — without relying on expensive short-term ad placements.

➔ Building a Business Worth Selling: You've stated clearly that your goal is to grow the business over the next decade and potentially sell it as a turnkey operation. Documented authority — a professional episode featuring your story and your work — can help strengthen the perceived and actual value of what you're offering to a future buyer or partner.

➔ Opening Doors to Strategic Partnerships: You mentioned that future partners are a real possibility — people or companies you haven't met yet. Visible, credible authority can help attract the kind of partnership conversations that don't happen through cold outreach, putting you in front of an audience already primed to take you seriously.

➔ Separating Yourself in a Crowded Market: In contracting, price is often the deciding factor when nothing else differentiates the bidders. A documentary can help shift the conversation from price comparison to trust and reputation, giving potential clients a reason to choose you before the first conversation even starts.

➔ Creating Something That Outlasts the Grind: You were clear that you don't want to simply retire and step away from everything you've built. A permanent, professional record of your story and your work can serve as a lasting asset for your business, your family, and the legacy you're still in the process of building.

We do not guarantee exact outcomes - results may vary!

YOUR AUTHORITY ASSET
Most businesses create content.
Very few create authority assets.
A documentary is not simply content.
It becomes an asset that can be used for years.
Your episode has the potential to become:
✓ A trust-building asset
✓ A credibility asset
✓ A speaking asset
✓ A sales asset
✓ A recruitment asset
✓ A referral asset
✓ A PR asset
✓ A social media asset
✓ A personal brand asset
✓ A legacy asset
The documentary becomes the foundation.
Everything else is built around it.

YOUR FAME STACK
One story can become hundreds of authority-building opportunities.
From a single episode we can create:
✓ Social media content
✓ Podcast content
✓ PR opportunities
✓ Blog content
✓ Speaking opportunities
✓ Website content
✓ Sales assets
✓ Recruitment assets
✓ Thought leadership content
✓ Future media opportunities
The episode is not the destination.
It is the beginning.
One story.
Distributed everywhere.
Repeated consistently.
This is how authority is built.
This is how industry fame is built.

WHY WE BELIEVE YOU ARE A FIT
We believe your story has the potential to:
✓ Educate others
✓ Inspire others
✓ Build trust
✓ Strengthen your authority
✓ Increase your visibility
✓ Position you as a leader within your category
Most importantly...
We believe your story deserves to be told.

Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.

Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You built your love for cheesecakes the way the best things are built — quietly, in a home kitchen, during a time when the world slowed down and you had space to discover what you were made of. With your partner by your side, you started experimenting with recipes, feeding each other, and chasing a craft that felt like more than a hobby. That passion became a business, rooted in your community, your Caribbean family heritage, and a street with a story the whole world already knows.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...

But passion alone doesn't scale a business. You still work armed security to keep the lights on. Life is expensive. Food is expensive. And every day, the dream waits on resources that haven't arrived yet.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

The business found its footing on the street where the film Friday was shot, where your friend owns the house and visitors come to take pictures. Your cheesecakes became part of that experience. When the Rams came through, you fed them — and they told you to keep going. That kind of validation doesn't come from a marketing plan. It comes from earning it.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

You grew up with limited resources and credit street-level hustle for skills that later translated into high-end sales. v2_1793962416336_ummx8p39.draft_text:
INSIDE SUCCESS TV
CONDITIONAL CASTING APPROVAL
Mirna Ashaka
Potential Feature for Inside Success TV

CONGRATULATIONS
After reviewing your application, story, business, and vision, our casting team believes you may be an exceptional fit for an upcoming season of Inside Success TV.
We do not select guests simply because they own a business.
We look for founders, experts, entrepreneurs, professionals and industry leaders who have:
✓ A meaningful story
✓ Genuine expertise
✓ A clear mission
✓ Real-world impact
✓ The potential to inspire others
Based on our review, we believe your story contains the key ingredients of a compelling Inside Success TV episode.
As a result, you have received conditional approval to continue through the casting process.

WHY YOUR STORY STANDS OUT
Most businesses have products.
The most successful brands have stories.
Your story is not simply about what you do.
It is about why you do it.
The strongest episodes are never about a company.
They are about a mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe your story has the potential to educate, inspire and position you as a trusted authority within your industry.

YOUR HOLLYWOOD STORY FORMULA
Every great documentary follows a proven storytelling structure.
Hollywood has used this formula for decades because people remember stories far more than facts.
Here's how we currently see your story unfolding.

ACT 1: THE ORDINARY WORLD
You started with a single idea, a credit card, and $1,000. At 21 years old, you launched a catering business during one of the most uncertain moments in recent history — right in the middle of COVID and the shutdown. Most people were waiting for the world to open back up. You were building something inside it.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...
There was a person trying to solve a problem that mattered.

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
Starting a food business from scratch, with minimal capital, during a global pandemic, in a market that had shut down almost entirely — the odds were stacked against you from day one. There was no roadmap, no safety net, and no guarantee anyone would show up. You had to earn every event, every client, and every dollar through sheer persistence.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
Your first year, you worked 50 events. As the world reopened, you pushed that to 150 to 200 events a year. You learned the business from your brother, brought it from San Diego to Michigan, and built it on word of mouth, honest service, and hard work. Six years in, you had grown from a one-person operation to a team of over 20 employees, and you expanded into a food truck under the Detroit Royal Eats name. You have since purchased two more Sprinter vans to convert into dessert trucks — each step funded by the one before it.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

ACT 4: THE BREAKTHROUGH
What began as a $1,000 bet on yourself grew into a business generating $150,000 to $200,000 a year. You built a client base across corporate events, weddings, bridal showers, communions, baptisms, and birthdays. Your story earned you features on Fox 2, Channel 7, Channel 4, and articles including one out of Los Angeles — without spending a dollar to get there. The visibility found you because the work was real.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

ACT 5: THE LEGACY
Your goal was never just to run a successful catering business. It was to prove something — that a woman, starting young, starting with almost nothing, can build something that matters. You want to franchise what you have built, and more than that, you want every young woman who sees your story to understand that the starting point does not define the destination. That mission is what makes your story bigger than any single event you have ever catered.
This is where your story becomes bigger than you.
Not just what you've built.
But what you're trying to change.
The lives you want to impact.
The movement you want to create.

YOUR THING
The most memorable brands become known for one thing.
One clear idea.
One clear promise.
One clear mission.
After reviewing your application, we believe the territory your brand has the opportunity to own is:
"The young woman who turned $1,000 into a food empire — and is just getting started"
This becomes the foundation of authority.
The thing people remember.
The thing they repeat.
The thing that eventually becomes synonymous with your name.

THE MISSION YOU ARE BUILDING
The strongest brands don't simply sell services.
They stand for something.
They fight against something.
They create movements.
Based on our review, we believe your mission includes:
✓ You believe that women, especially young women, do not need permission or a perfect starting point to build something powerful — they need proof that it is possible.
✓ You stand for the idea that starting small is not a limitation; it is the foundation of every real success story worth telling.
✓ You are building toward a future where the business you created from a credit card and a dream becomes a franchise — a model others can follow.
✓ You fight for the visibility of entrepreneurs who grow through community, service, and word of mouth rather than big budgets and inherited advantages.
✓ Your deeper mission is to show that hard work, honesty, and showing up for your community can take you from your first $1,000 to a legacy that outlasts any single truck, event, or year.
This is bigger than marketing.
This is bigger than business.
This is legacy.

WHY THIS STORY MATTERS NOW
We live in a world where consumers have more choices than ever before.
The challenge isn't having the best product.
The challenge is being remembered.
People buy from brands they trust.
People trust brands they remember.
People remember stories.
This is why your story matters.
Not because it is interesting.
Because it has the potential to build trust at scale.

For you, specifically, that can look like:

➔ Expanding Beyond Your Local Market: You have built strong recognition in your community, and your goal is to grow the brand toward festivals, fairs, schools, and eventually a franchise. A documentary-style episode can help increase visibility well beyond the Detroit area, reaching audiences who may never have discovered you through local word of mouth alone.

➔ Building the Kind of Authority That Supports Franchising: If franchising is on your horizon, being known and trusted at a broader level matters. A dedicated episode telling your full story can help strengthen your positioning as a credible, established brand — the kind of story that can support conversations with future partners, investors, or franchise candidates.

➔ Turning Your Story Into a Marketing Asset: You have already earned media coverage without paying for it, because your story is compelling. A full documentary episode can become an evergreen asset you use across your website, social media, and pitches — something that works for your brand long after the initial release.

➔ Standing Out in a Crowded Food and Events Market: Corporate clients, event planners, and vendors have choices. Being featured on a television network can help differentiate your business in a way that a social media post or local news clip cannot — giving potential clients a reason to choose you before they ever make a call.

➔ Giving Your Mission a Bigger Stage: You said it clearly: if you did it, other women can do it. A platform that reaches a national audience can help amplify that message, connecting your personal mission of inspiring young women entrepreneurs to people far beyond the community where you first built your name.

We do not guarantee exact outcomes - results may vary!

YOUR AUTHORITY ASSET
Most businesses create content.
Very few create authority assets.
A documentary is not simply content.
It becomes an asset that can be used for years.
Your episode has the potential to become:
✓ A trust-building asset
✓ A credibility asset
✓ A speaking asset
✓ A sales asset
✓ A recruitment asset
✓ A referral asset
✓ A PR asset
✓ A social media asset
✓ A personal brand asset
✓ A legacy asset
The documentary becomes the foundation.
Everything else is built around it.

YOUR FAME STACK
One story can become hundreds of authority-building opportunities.
From a single episode we can create:
✓ Social media content
✓ Podcast content
✓ PR opportunities
✓ Blog content
✓ Speaking opportunities
✓ Website content
✓ Sales assets
✓ Recruitment assets
✓ Thought leadership content
✓ Future media opportunities
The episode is not the destination.
It is the beginning.
One story.
Distributed everywhere.
Repeated consistently.
This is how authority is built.
This is how industry fame is built.

WHY WE BELIEVE YOU ARE A FIT
We believe your story has the potential to:
✓ Educate others
✓ Inspire others
✓ Build trust
✓ Strengthen your authority
✓ Increase your visibility
✓ Position you as a leader within your category
Most importantly...
We believe your story deserves to be told.

NEXT STEP

• The vision for your episode
• Potential positioning opportunities

Failure to attend may result in your application being withdrawn from the current casting cycle.

Your crew isn't made up of résumé hires — most of your team came straight out of incarceration, because you know what it means to need someone to believe in you. This is where your expertise was earned.

You came into this world without a blueprint for safety or stability. Born to a teenage mother and raised in an environment shaped by addiction, criminal activity, and generational hardship, the life around you normalized chaos long before you were old enough to question it. By fifteen, alcohol had already taken hold, and the pain of being told you would likely never become a mother sent you deeper into substances. You were not running from life — you were surviving the only way you had ever been shown how.
Before the business existed...
Before the recognition...
Before the growth...

ACT 2: THE CHALLENGE
The turning point did not arrive gently. At twenty-nine, your sister's postpartum crisis ended in tragedy — her infant daughter gone at three weeks old — and no amount of substances could touch that grief. The pain cracked something open that could not be closed again. You made a decision: if you could not have your own children, you would at least become a person worthy of honoring the ones you had lost. Two months into sobriety, you discovered you were pregnant — the very thing doctors had told you would never happen. That impossible moment became the foundation everything else was built on.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.
The challenge became the catalyst.

ACT 3: THE JOURNEY
Sobriety did not hand you a clear path — it handed you a willingness to keep walking without one. You waited tables, listened to business conversations happening around you, and wrote your dreams into a notebook at work. You got married, built a family, and then faced your husband's cancer diagnosis in the same season you launched your wedding business. You had a mental breakdown, received a borderline personality disorder diagnosis, entered intensive treatment, and kept booking clients anyway. You reached out to mentors in the wedding industry, leaned into dialectical skills to build better relationships, and refused to let not knowing what you were doing stop you from showing up at the highest level you could.
This is where your expertise was earned.
Not through theory.
Through experience.
Through years of learning what actually works.

People from the recovery community are asking to join your team. Clients are changing their wedding dates just to book with you personally, and your business continues to grow primarily through referrals and word of mouth. What started as a server's notebook full of handwritten dreams is now a touring wedding business with dates listed on your website and clients booking into the following year at a rapid rate.
This is the proof.
The moment your philosophy, method or vision began producing real-world results.
The evidence that your mission matters.

The goal is to be a living demonstration that the same grit it took to survive a dangerous life can be redirected into something that blesses everyone it touches.

You had the technical expertise, but the business knowledge wasn't there, and no amount of grinding could substitute for the systems, coaching, and community you hadn't yet found. You were working in the business so hard that you couldn't work on it.
This was the turning point.
The moment where staying the same was no longer an option.

The turning point came when you stopped trying to figure it out alone. You leaned into business coaching and joined a community of other automotive shop owners who had already walked the road you were on. They showed you where the potholes were, helped you build confidence, and gave you a framework to lead rather than just labor. It wasn't fast, and it wasn't easy, but you committed, meeting weekly, connecting with peers, and traveling to group gatherings multiple times a year to sharpen your thinking and your operation.
This is where your expertise was earned.

Through years of learning what actually works.

The business held. Your manager led. And you were exactly where your family needed you to be.
This is the proof.

You want them to know that building a business that works without you is not a dream reserved for MBA graduates. After reviewing your application, business background, accomplishments, personality, and overall fit, our casting team believes you could be a strong fit for an upcoming reality show on Inside Success TV.
Our reality shows feature successful entrepreneurs, business owners, founders, and high-performing personalities who are willing to put their experience, decision-making, leadership, and business skills to the test.

✅ A competitive personality

Based on our initial review, we believe you have several of the qualities our production team is looking for.

Based on what we learned during the application process, our casting team currently sees several qualities that could make you an interesting addition to an upcoming production.
BUSINESS EXPERIENCE
You are in an active growth phase, recently expanding into two states you were not operating in before. You hired and made staffing adjustments along the way, and you describe yourself as now fully in a becoming stage, pushing forward after working through a difficult stretch.
COMPETITIVE EDGE
You read group dynamics fast and adjust your approach accordingly, holding back when others are overreaching and stepping up when no one else does. When you pushed back on a hypothetical bad plan, you framed it as a strategy question, not a power move, which shows real situational intelligence.
PERSONALITY
You are light and funny but shift to direct and no-nonsense the moment the stakes rise. You said it yourself: you know how to get things done, pull people together, and stay focused without taking yourself too seriously.
THE WILDCARD
You described yourself as a sleeper, someone who conserves energy and waits for the right moment. That patience, combined with the directness you showed when pushed, could make you genuinely unpredictable to other cast members who misjudge you early.
These are some of the qualities our production team will explore further during the next stage of casting.

Most businesses create content.

Together, they create a powerful foundation for building visibility, credibility, and authority around your brand.
